Adapted from Analysis 2 (Created by ChatGPT). Doing this analysis for **Joe Costello (Exeter)** to see how the peroxisomal biology is effected in LTP knockouts. I will follow a
previous prompt by ChatGPT:

1.  LPC 26:0

-   Abundance; optionally LPC 26:0/LPC 22:0
-   A particularly useful starting marker for VLCFA accumulation

2.  VLCFA-containing lipids

-   Species containing 24:0, 26:0, or 26:1, analyzed separately within
    each lipid class
-   Look for a coordinated shift toward longer chains

3.  Chain-length ratios

-   C26:0-containing/C22:0-containing species within the same class

4.  Ether PC and PE

-   Ether species relative to corresponding diacyl species; plasmalogens
    separately if resolved

5.  DHA-containing lipids:

-   Species with a confirmed 22:6 chain

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# 1. Setup

```{R}
# ============================================================
# LTP KO LIBRARY
# COMPOSITIONAL LIPID + SATURATION REMODELLING ANALYSIS
# ============================================================

library(tidyverse)
library(ggrepel)
library(ggthemes)
library(ggbeeswarm)
library(reshape2)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = F,warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,fig.width = 10,fig.height = 7
)

theme_set(
  theme_base(base_size = 10) +
    theme(
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95")
    )
)

options(dplyr.summarise.inform = FALSE)


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# SETTINGS
# ------------------------------------------------------------


CONTROL_GENES <- paste0("NonTarget_", 1:6)  
REFERENCE_MODE <- "controls"

EXCLUDE_GENES <- c(
  # "GENE1",
  # "GENE2"
)

EXCLUDE_SAMPLE_KEYS <- c(
  # "GENE1__Sample1__Extraction1__Roster1"
)


# Number of biological replicates we ideally want
MIN_REPLICATES <- 2

# Replicate correlation below this is worth inspecting.
MIN_REPLICATE_CORRELATION <- 0.70


# Compensation thresholds.
# A class is considered "stable" when its abundance differs
# by less than:
# max(1 percentage point, 20% of its reference abundance)

CLASS_STABILITY_MIN_PP <- 1
CLASS_STABILITY_RELATIVE <- 0.20


# At least this much of the within-class saturation
# distribution must be rearranged.

MIN_REDISTRIBUTION_PERCENT <- 10

# Replicate saturation profiles should point in approximately
# the same direction.

MIN_PROFILE_AGREEMENT <- 0.50


# Heatmap sizes
TOP_N_SPECIES <- 50
```

# 2. Prepare the raw data

```{R}
# ============================================================
# DATA PREPARATION
# ============================================================
acyls1 = read_csv("../data/LTP_acyl_concentrations_raw1.csv")
#acyls1 = read_csv("data/LTP_acyl_concentrations_raw1.csv")
#acyls1 = read_csv("data/LTP_acyl_concentrations_raw1.csv")

acyls1 <- acyls1 %>% 
   mutate(X = paste0(Class, "(",Tails,")")) 


acyls_raw <- acyls1[-1] %>%
   mutate(
      Gene = as.character(Target.Gene.Symbol), 
      LipidSpecies = as.character(X),
      Class = as.character(Class),
      nmol = as.numeric(nmolg), 
      TotalDB = as.numeric(Total_tail_bend), 
      TotalLength = as.numeric(Total_tail_length),
      Tail1DB = as.numeric(Tail_1_bend),
      Tail2DB = as.numeric(Tail_2_bend),
      Tail1Length = as.numeric(Tail_1_length),
      Tail2Length = as.numeric(Tail_2_length),
      ExpectedTails = readr::parse_number(as.character(Tails)),
      Group = if_else(Gene %in% CONTROL_GENES, "CTRL", "KO"),
      SampleKey = paste(Gene, SampleID, Extraction, Roster, sep = "__"),
      Feature = paste(Class, LipidSpecies, sep = " | ")
   ) %>%
   filter(!is.na(Gene),
          !is.na(Class),
          !is.na(LipidSpecies),
          is.finite(nmol),
          nmol >= 0)
```

Check the samples:

```{R}
acyls_raw %>% 
  distinct(
    Gene, SampleID, Extraction, Roster, SampleKey
  ) %>%
  arrange(Gene,SampleID) %>%
  print(n = Inf)
```

# 3. Function for within-sample normalization

This is now the core of the analysis.

```{R}
make_species_table <- function(dat) {

  dat %>%

    group_by(
      SampleKey,
      Gene,
      Group,
      LBP_Family,
      SampleID,
      Extraction,
      Roster,
      Type2,
      Class,
      LipidSpecies,
      Feature,
      Tails,
      Tail_1,
      Tail1Length,
      Tail1DB,
      Tail_2,
      Tail2Length,
      Tail2DB,
      TotalLength,
      TotalDB,
      ExpectedTails
    ) %>%

    summarise(
      nmol =
        sum(
          nmol,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%

    # ---------------------------------
    # FIRST NORMALIZATION:
    # each species as fraction of
    # the complete sample lipidome
    # ---------------------------------

    group_by(
      SampleKey
    ) %>%

    mutate(
      SampleTotalNmol =sum(nmol,na.rm = TRUE),
      SampleMolFraction = nmol / SampleTotalNmol,
      SampleMolPct =
        100 *
        SampleMolFraction
    ) %>%

    ungroup() %>%

    # ---------------------------------
    # SECOND NORMALIZATION:
    # species as fraction of its class
    #
    # This is used for saturation
    # redistribution / compensation.
    # ---------------------------------

    group_by(
      SampleKey,
      Class
    ) %>%

    mutate(

      ClassNmol =
        sum(
          nmol,
          na.rm = TRUE
        ),

      ClassMolPct =
        100 *
        ClassNmol /
        first(
          SampleTotalNmol
        ),

      WithinClassFraction =
        nmol /
        ClassNmol,

      WithinClassPct =
        100 *
        WithinClassFraction
    ) %>%

    ungroup()
}
```

Initial normalization, before exclusions:

```{R}
species_initial <-
  make_species_table(
    acyls_raw
  )



```

Check that each sample sums to 100%:

```{R}
species_initial %>%
  group_by(
    SampleKey
  ) %>%
  summarise(
    TotalPct =
      sum(
        SampleMolPct
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  summary()
```

These should all be approximately `100`.

# 4. QC before excluding anything

Because the analysis is compositional, I would assess replicate
similarity using a **CLR-like transformation of the within-sample
proportions**, rather than raw nmol.

```{R}
# ============================================================
# QC
# ============================================================

clr_transform <- function(x) {
  x <- as.numeric(x)
  positive <-
    x[
      is.finite(x) &
      x > 0
    ]
  if (length(positive) == 0) {
    return(
      rep(
        0,
        length(x)
      )
    )
  }

  pseudo <-
    min(positive) / 2
  lx <-
    log(
      x +
      pseudo
    )

  lx -
    mean(lx)
}


safe_cor <- function(x, y) {
  ok <-
    is.finite(x) & is.finite(y)

  if (sum(ok) < 5)
    return(NA_real_)

  if (
    sd(x[ok]) == 0 || sd(y[ok]) == 0
  )
    return(NA_real_)

  cor(
    x[ok],
    y[ok],
    method = "spearman"
  )
}
```

Create sample × species matrix:

```{R}
qc_wide <- species_initial %>%
  group_by(
    SampleKey,
    Feature
  ) %>%

  summarise(
    SampleMolPct =
      sum(
        SampleMolPct
      ),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

  pivot_wider(
    names_from =
      Feature,
    values_from =
      SampleMolPct,
    values_fill = 0
  )


qc_ids <-
  qc_wide$SampleKey


qc_matrix <-
  qc_wide %>%
  select(
    -SampleKey
  ) %>%
  as.matrix()


rownames(qc_matrix) <- qc_ids


qc_clr <-
  t(
    apply(
      qc_matrix,
      1,
      clr_transform
    )
  )
```

Sample metadata:

```{R}
sample_metadata <- species_initial %>%
  distinct(
    SampleKey,
    Gene,
    Group,
    SampleID,
    Extraction,
    Roster,
    LBP_Family
  )
```

# 5. Replicate-to-consensus correlation

For every replicate, compare its lipidome with the median of the other
replicates for that same LTP.

```{R}
replicate_correlations <-
  map_dfr(
    unique(
      sample_metadata$Gene
    ),

    function(gene_i) {

      ids <-
        sample_metadata %>%
        filter(
          Gene == gene_i
        ) %>%
        pull(
          SampleKey
        )


      if (length(ids) < 2) {

        return(
          tibble(
            SampleKey = ids,
            ReplicateConsensusR =
              NA_real_
          )
        )
      }


      map_dfr(

        ids,

        function(id_i) {

          other_ids <-
            setdiff(
              ids,
              id_i
            )


          consensus <-
            apply(
              qc_clr[
                other_ids,
                ,
                drop = FALSE
              ],
              2,
              median,
              na.rm = TRUE
            )


          tibble(

            SampleKey =
              id_i,

            ReplicateConsensusR =
              safe_cor(
                qc_clr[
                  id_i,
                ],
                consensus
              )
          )
        }
      )
    }
  )
```

Sample totals:

```{R Sample totals}
qc_summary <- species_initial %>%

  group_by(
    SampleKey,
    Gene,
    Group,
    SampleID
  ) %>%

  summarise(

    TotalNmol =
      first(
        SampleTotalNmol
      ),

    DetectedSpecies =
      sum(
        nmol > 0
      ),

    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%

  left_join(
    replicate_correlations,
    by = "SampleKey"
  ) %>%

  mutate(

    BadReplicate =
      !is.na(
        ReplicateConsensusR
      ) &
      ReplicateConsensusR <
        MIN_REPLICATE_CORRELATION
  )
```

Plot:

```{R}
ggplot(
  qc_summary,
  aes(x = Gene, y = ReplicateConsensusR)) +
   geom_hline(yintercept = MIN_REPLICATE_CORRELATION, linetype = 2 ) +
  geom_point(aes(shape =BadReplicate),
    position =position_jitter(width = 0.15), size = 2.5) +
  geom_text_repel(data =
                     qc_summary %>%
                     filter(BadReplicate),
                  aes(label =paste0(Gene," / ",SampleID)),
                  size = 3,max.overlaps = Inf) +
   coord_flip() +
   labs(title ="Reproducibility of within-sample-normalized lipidomes",
        x = NULL,y ="Correlation with other replicates")
```

This is where I would identify the obviously non-reproducible samples.

Print their exact keys:

```{R}
qc_summary %>%
   filter(BadReplicate) %>%
   select(Gene,SampleID,SampleKey,ReplicateConsensusR) %>%
   arrange(ReplicateConsensusR) %>%
   print(n = Inf)
```

Then put the problematic ones into `EXCLUDE_SAMPLE_KEYS` at the top.

# 6. Apply exclusions and renormalize

This renormalization step is important: if a complete sample is removed,
no issue. The percentages of the remaining samples are calculated
independently anyway.

```{R}
EXCLUDE_SAMPLE_KEYS = c(
   "COL4A3BP__K90__K__90",
   "GLTPD2__H45__H__45",
   "SEC14L2__J49__J__49"
)

acyls_clean <- acyls_raw %>%
  filter(
    !Gene %in% EXCLUDE_GENES,
    !SampleKey %in% EXCLUDE_SAMPLE_KEYS
  )

species <-
  make_species_table(
    acyls_clean
  )


#anti_join(acyls_raw, acyls_clean) %>% View

```

## Analysis 2: VLCFA-containing lipids
- Species containing 24:0, 26:0, or 26:1, analyzed separately within each lipid class
- Look for a coordinated shift toward longer chains


```{R}
species_gene %>% 
  filter(!Class == 'PA') %>% 
  filter(Tail_1 > 230) %>% 
  ggplot(aes(LipidSpecies, MedianWithinClassPct)) +
  #ggplot(aes(Class, MedianSampleMolPct)) +
  facet_wrap(.~LipidSpecies, scales = 'free') +
  geom_quasirandom() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        aspect.ratio = 1) +
  labs(title = 'All lipids with VLCFA',
       y = 'Median within Class Percentage')

# Set the number of top/bottom points you want to highlight
N = 3

species_gene %>% 
  filter(Class != 'PA', Tail_1 > 230) %>% 
  group_by(LipidSpecies) %>% 
  mutate(
    rank_desc = row_number(desc(MedianWithinClassPct)), # 1 = Highest
    rank_asc  = row_number(MedianWithinClassPct),       # 1 = Lowest
    highlight_type = case_when(
      rank_desc <= N ~ "Top N",
      rank_asc  <= N ~ "Bottom N",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  ggplot(aes(LipidSpecies, MedianWithinClassPct)) +
  geom_quasirandom(color = "grey60", alpha = 0.7) +
  # Highlight the top and bottom points with colored dots
  # geom_point(
  #   data = . %>% filter(!is.na(highlight_type)),
  #   aes(color = highlight_type),
  #   size = 2.5
  # ) +
  # Add text labels for the highlighted points
  geom_text_repel(
    data = . %>% filter(!is.na(highlight_type)),
    aes(label = Gene, color = highlight_type),
    size = 3.5,
    max.overlaps = Inf, # Ensures labels aren't hidden due to crowding
    box.padding = 0.5,
    point.padding = 0.3, 
    nudge_x = 1
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Top N" = "firebrick", "Bottom N" = "dodgerblue")) +
  facet_wrap(~LipidSpecies, scales = 'free') +
  #theme_minimal() +
  #labs(color = "Highlighted") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        aspect.ratio = 0.5) +
  labs(title = 'All lipids with VLCFA',
       y = 'Median within Class Percentage')
```

## Analysis 3: Chain-length ratios

C26:0-containing/C22:0-containing species within the same class

```{R}

  
species_long2short = species %>%
  filter(!Class == 'PA') %>% 
  filter(!Class == 'TAG') %>% 
  filter(Tail1Length %in% c(22, 26)) %>% 
  group_by(
    SampleKey,
    Gene,
    Class,
    Tail1DB) %>% 
  dcast(SampleKey+Gene+Class+Tail1DB ~ Tail1Length, 
        value.var = 'nmol',
        fill = 0) %>% 
  mutate(LongToShortRatio = `26`/`22`) %>% 
  filter(! LongToShortRatio == 0) %>% 
  filter(! LongToShortRatio == Inf) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  
  group_by(
    Gene,
    Class,
    Tail1DB,
  ) %>%
  
  # Step 3: Summarize centered data (MedianSampleMolPct_Centered will evaluate to 0)
  summarise(
    n = n_distinct(SampleKey),
    
    Median_LongToShortRatio = median(LongToShortRatio, na.rm = TRUE),
    Deviation_LongToShortRatio = sd(LongToShortRatio, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) 
  
  

N = 3

species_long2short %>% 
  group_by(Class, Tail1DB) %>% 
  mutate(
    rank_desc = row_number(desc(Median_LongToShortRatio)), # 1 = Highest
    rank_asc  = row_number(Median_LongToShortRatio),       # 1 = Lowest
    highlight_type = case_when(
      rank_desc <= N ~ "Top N",
      rank_asc  <= N ~ "Bottom N",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  ggplot(aes(1, Median_LongToShortRatio)) +
  facet_wrap(Class~Tail1DB, scale = 'free') +
  geom_quasirandom(color = "grey60", alpha = 0.7) +
  # Highlight the top and bottom points with colored dots
  # geom_point(
  #   data = . %>% filter(!is.na(highlight_type)),
  #   aes(color = highlight_type),
  #   size = 2.5
  # ) +
  # Add text labels for the highlighted points
  geom_text_repel(
    data = . %>% filter(!is.na(highlight_type)),
    aes(label = Gene, color = highlight_type),
    size = 3.5,
    max.overlaps = Inf, # Ensures labels aren't hidden due to crowding
    box.padding = 0.5,
    point.padding = 0.3, 
    nudge_x = 1
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Top N" = "firebrick", "Bottom N" = "dodgerblue")) 


```


## Analysis 4:  Ether PC and PE

-   Ether species relative to corresponding diacyl species; plasmalogens separately if resolved


```{R}
#zscore function
z.score = 
  function(x) {
    Score = (x - mean(x, na.rm = T)) - sd(x, na.rm = T)
    # if(is.infinite(Score))
    #   return(NA)
    # else
    return(Score)
  
}


#grouped by Tail_1 as it is the O- or P- linked tail.

species.ether = 
  species %>%  
  filter(Class %in% c('PE','PEP','PEO')) %>% 
  group_by(
    SampleKey,
    Gene, 
    Roster,
    Tail_1,
    Class
  ) %>% 
  summarise(tails.sum.nmol = sum(nmol, na.rm = T)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  dcast(
    SampleKey+Gene+Roster+Tail_1~Class,
    value.var = 'tails.sum.nmol'
  ) %>% 
  group_by(Gene, Roster, Tail_1) %>% 
  summarise(meanPEO2PE = mean(PEO/PE, na.rm = T),
            meanPEP2PE = mean(PEP/PE, na.rm = T)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  group_by(Tail_1) %>% 
  mutate(
    z.peo.2.pe.ratio = z.score(meanPEO2PE),
    z.pep.2.pe.ratio = z.score(meanPEP2PE)
  ) 
  
N = 3
species.ether %>% 
  group_by(Tail_1) %>% 
  mutate(
    rank_desc = row_number(desc(meanPEP2PE)), # 1 = Highest
    rank_asc  = row_number(meanPEP2PE),       # 1 = Lowest
    highlight_type = case_when(
      rank_desc <= N ~ "Top N",
      rank_asc  <= N ~ "Bottom N",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  ) %>% 
  #filter( Tail_1 == 161) %>% 
  #filter(Roster < 3) %>% 
  ggplot(
    aes(1, meanPEP2PE
    )
  ) +
  facet_wrap(.~Tail_1, scales = 'free_y',nrow = 1) +
  #geom_boxplot(aes(group = Roster)) +
  #geom_line(group) + 
  geom_quasirandom() +
  geom_text_repel(
    data = . %>% filter(!is.na(highlight_type)),
    aes(label = Gene, color = highlight_type),
    size = 3.5,
    max.overlaps = Inf, # Ensures labels aren't hidden due to crowding
    box.padding = 0.5,
    point.padding = 0.3, 
    nudge_x = 2
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Top N" = "firebrick", "Bottom N" = "dodgerblue")) 
  



```


## Analysis 5:  DHA-containing lipids



```{R}



#Check the total % of DHA-containing lipids
species.DHA = 
  species %>%  
  filter(Tail_1 == 226 | Tail_2 == 226) %>% 
  group_by(
    SampleKey,
    Gene, 
    Roster,
  ) %>% 
  summarise(dha.total.perc = sum(SampleMolPct, na.rm = T)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  group_by(Gene, Roster) %>% 
  summarise(meanDHA = mean(dha.total.perc, na.rm = T),
            sdDHA = sd(dha.total.perc, na.rm = T)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(
    z.DHA = z.score(meanDHA)
  )
```
